industry.why: Neutral, carried, balanced on new evidence both ways. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment and grid, Diversified groups, Distributors and Test and measurement at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Counter-case for B: the order data are the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack; for D: the tape and the regime.

sector.key: O.18. Test, measurement, sensing and safety technology
sector.why: Neutral, set deliberately this week (carried C). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): regulated, recurring test and measurement demand is the proven case the regime pays for, but the group's growth leg is semiconductor and industrial capital spending, which the week de-rated; Jenoptik's memo (Mixed) states it exactly: the order book is the demand case and the 69th-percentile multiple after a doubling is the valuation case. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: B now, C prior. Three MI Pool names (Vaisala, Jenoptik, Renishaw). Counter-case for higher: relative strength improving and Renishaw's five-of-eight A or B; for lower: the semiconductor exposure now sits under an Underweight sector. Balanced; Neutral by judgement.

geography.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 and energy leading the week; Norway is where the energy hedge is listed (Equinor, Aker BP, Var Energi, Odfjell Drilling, Subsea 7, TGS in the Pool). Oslo's own performance was not re-read this week. Relative strength is not graded by country. Counter-case: this double counts the Energy rows for most of the 46 Norwegian stocks; back to C if Brent falls under $85 or Oslo's leadership reverses for four weeks.
